newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to join EU in challenging U.S. law on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Canada to join EU in challenging U.S. law on Cuba.

text.p: Canada has decided to join the European Union at the World Trade Organisation in challenging the United States' new anti-Cuban legislation, Canadian trade spokesman Charles Larabie said on Wednesday.

"The Americans now have a law in place which we firmly believe is in contravention of the WTO and NAFTA (the North American Free Trade Agreement) as well, so we will take them to court, so to speak, on that basis," Larabie said.
European Union foreign ministers decided on Tuesday to request a dispute panel at a WTO meeting in Geneva on Oct. 16, challenging the Helms-Burton act, passed in July.
"We're going to join them as an interested third party," Larabie said.

Helms-Burton, passed after Cuba shot down two civilian U.S. aircraft off the Cuban coast in February, allows Americans -- including former Cubans -- to sue foreign firms using property seized after the 1959 revolution in Cuba.

President Bill Clinton has suspended that particular provision for six months, but the law also provides for dthe barring from the United States of senior executives of such companies, as well as their families.
Larabie said Canada still planned to file a challenge under NAFTA. "It's a question of when we're going to do it," he said.
He said Canada could not be the main complainant in both forums, so it was joining the EU complaint as a third party.
It could take six to eight months for the WTO process to be completed, he said.
